cases.name: the-sweep-at-count-equals-n-is-a-permutation-of-the-sample
cases.description: The sharpest single test of where an observation sits on the ruler. With count equal to the sample size, slot i reads (i + 0.5) / n, which lands on observation i exactly — so the run returns the sample itself, reordered, with every repeat kept: three 12s and two 25s come back as three and two. Under the older i/(n-1) placement this cannot hold: the ends would double up and something in the middle would go missing. Guards the fix, and guards it in ten lines.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="sweep" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="file" src="sample-repeats.txt" read="quantile" sample="exact"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: between-observations-the-sweep-invents-the-middle
cases.description: Twice as many rows as observations, so half the slots fall between two neighbours and take a value the sample never held (14, 17, 21, …). This is the cure for the comb, made visible: the file has ten values, the run has fifteen. If a port ever reverts to picking nearest observations, this case breaks and the one above still passes.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="sweep" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="file" src="sample-repeats.txt" read="quantile" sample="exact"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-dense-value-keeps-its-share-an-isolated-one-dissolves
cases.description: Eight observations, EVERY ONE of multiplicity one, so multiplicity cannot explain anything here. Four stand one apart (10, 11, 12, 13) and four stand far apart (40, 80, 160, 320). The dense ones come back at exactly their share — two rows each out of sixteen — while 40, 80 and 160 do not appear at all: their mass went to the values inside the gaps. This is the property the docs describe, and it is about the distance to the neighbour, not about how often a value repeats.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="16" seed="gaps" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="file" src="sample-gaps.txt" read="quantile" sample="exact"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: with-no-gaps-every-share-is-exact
cases.description: The consequence of the case above, stated positively: 1..5 with nothing missing between them, twenty-five rows, five of each. When a sample has no holes at its own step, the quantile read is not an approximation of the shares — it is exact. This is the test a user can run on their own file before choosing between read="quantile" and weight=.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="25" seed="five" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="file" src="sample-dense.txt" read="quantile" sample="exact"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-big-atom-survives-the-ramps-at-its-edges
cases.description: Six of ten observations are exactly zero. The plateau dominates, so the atom comes back — eleven rows of twenty rather than the twelve its 60% would ask for, the difference being the ramp from 0 up to its neighbour 2. Pins the honest middle ground: big atoms survive, they do not survive to the last row.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="atom" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="file" src="sample-atom.txt" read="quantile" sample="exact"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-dice-path-over-the-same-gaps
cases.description: The same file without sample="exact", so each row throws its own dice. Pins the ordinary path against the same shape, and pins that the two paths are different runs rather than the same numbers reordered.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="16" seed="gaps" local="en"><sequence name="OUT"><gen type="file" src="sample-gaps.txt" read="quantile"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{OUT}}</data></line></block></tdc>
